# Study Notes: computer network Stllbus.pdf

## Overview
These study notes cover the syllabus for **CSE306: Computer Networks**, spanning 6 structured units, corresponding course outcomes (CO1 to CO6), practical experiments using Cisco Packet Tracer and CLI, and designated textbooks. The course focuses on network topologies, reference models, data communication, error handling, MAC protocols, IP addressing, routing algorithms, transport layer services, congestion control, application layer protocols, and wireless networking standards.

---

## Important Concepts & Definitions

*   **Computer Networks & Hardware:** Introduction to networks, network hardware architecture, topologies, and core devices including **Hubs**, **Switches**, and **Routers**.
*   **Network Software Architecture:** Layered architectures, protocols, the **OSI Model**, and the **TCP/IP protocol suite**.
*   **Physical & Data Link Layers:** Data communication basics, guided and unguided transmission media, transmission impairments, and performance. Elementary data link protocols along with error detection and correction mechanisms (**Hamming code**, **CRC**, **Parity**, and **Checksum**).
*   **MAC Sublayer & Network Layer:** Multiple access protocols (**ALOHA**, **CSMA**, **CSMA/CD**) and the **Ethernet protocol**. IP addressing frameworks (both **Classful** and **Classless**), **Subnetting**, **FLSM**, and **VLSM**.
*   **Routing & IP Headers:** Routing algorithms including **Shortest path algorithm**, **Distance Vector Routing**, and **Link State Routing**. Structure of **IPv4** and **IPv6 Headers**, **IPv6 Addressing**, and **Network Address Translation (NAT)**.
*   **Transport Layer:** Relationship between the Transport and Network layers, services, performance issues, **TCP** (header format and handshaking operation), and **UDP** (header format).
*   **Congestion Control:** Network assistance congestion control algorithms and **TCP Congestion Control**.
*   **Application Layer & Wireless Networks:** Protocols including **Domain Name System (DNS)**, **E-mail**, and **FTP**. Wireless networks covering **IEEE 802.11 standards** (802.11a, 802.11b, 802.11g, 802.11n) and **Bluetooth** architecture and layers.

---

## Core Rules & Principles
*   **Error Detection and Correction Principles:** Employs mathematical and logical coding methods such as Hamming code, Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC), Parity bits, and Checksums to ensure data integrity during transmission.
*   **Addressing and Subnetting Principles:** Allocates network identifiers using both Classful and Classless addressing schemes, utilizing Variable-Length Subnet Masking (VLSM) and Fixed-Length Subnet Masking (FLSM) for efficient IP space utilization.
*   **Routing Principles:** Directs network traffic through static routing, dynamic routing (via Routing Information Protocol - RIP, RIP version 2), and advanced path determination algorithms (Shortest path, Distance Vector, Link State).
*   **Reliable Transport Principles:** Uses connection-oriented transmission via TCP (incorporating handshaking operations and header structuring) alongside connectionless transmission via UDP.

---

## Comparisons & Distinctions

| Feature / Mechanism | Classful / Static Routing & Addressing | Classless / Dynamic Routing (e.g., VLSM, RIP) | TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) | UDP (User Datagram Protocol) | IPv4 | IPv6 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Structure / Scope** | Fixed address boundaries; manually configured routes. | Flexible subnetting (FLSM/VLSM); dynamically updated via protocols like RIP. | Connection-oriented; includes handshaking and congestion control. | Connectionless; basic header format without handshaking. | Standard 32-bit address space with explicit header and NAT support. | Expanded address space with a dedicated IPv6 header format and direct routing. |

---

## Key Points
*   **Course Outcomes:** The curriculum is mapped across six learning objectives ranging from defining topologies and layers (CO1) to examining application layer protocols and wireless standards (CO6).
*   **Hardware & Simulation:** Utilizes Cisco Packet Tracer for practical lab work, covering cable creation (cross and straight), device port addition, and CLI command execution (`ipconfig`, `ping`, `tracert`, `arp`, `netstat`, `nslookup`, switch commands, and router commands).
*   **Server Configuration & LAN Setup:** Practical competencies include DHCP configuration, DNS, FTP, HTTP, Email server setup, and static/dynamic routing implementation for both IPv4 and IPv6.
*   **Core Literature:** Primary textbook is *DATA COMMUNICATIONS AND NETWORKING WITH TCP/IP PROTOCOL SUITE* by Behrouz A. Forouzan; reference text is *COMPUTER NETWORKS* by Andrew S. Tanenbaum.

---

## Revision Summary
*   **Architecture & Models:** Master the OSI model, TCP/IP protocol suite, network hardware (Hub, Switch, Router), and topologies (bus, star, ring, mesh, tree, hybrid).
*   **Protocols & Addressing:** Understand data link error handling (Hamming, CRC), MAC protocols (ALOHA, CSMA/CD), and Network layer IP addressing (Classful, Classless, Subnetting, NAT, IPv4/IPv6 headers).
*   **Routing & Transport:** Differentiate routing algorithms (Shortest path, Distance Vector, Link State) and transport mechanisms (TCP header/handshaking vs. UDP header, plus congestion control).
*   **Applications & Wireless:** Identify application services (DNS, E-mail, FTP) and wireless specifications (IEEE 802.11 variants and Bluetooth architecture).
